issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, but the provided solution implementation declares these attributes as int. This cross-artifact type mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to use and may lead to failing tests or unexpected casting/conversion issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int, or change the solution (and template) attributes and related methods to use double and adjust method return types/behavior accordingly.

issues.description: Within the problem statement's UML there is an internal inconsistency: the student-count attributes are typed as double while getTotalNumberOfStudents() is declared to return int. This contradiction leaves students unclear whether totals should be computed in floating-point or integer form.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and align numeric types in the UML/problem statement: either make the student-count attributes int so the total can be an int, or change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return double (and update its description) if fractional values are intended. Update all examples and hints to match the chosen approach.
